why: The other half of issue #492: adding a required ReplayMeta field WITHOUT bumping the schema, so a schema-3 trace recorded before the field existed is still accepted and replayed with the rule missing -- the exact silent divergence the field was added to stop, and the case the replay layer's no-migration policy answers by rejecting rather than defaulting. Invisible to every other assertion in the file, because `checkTrace` compares a trace's stamp against this same constant and the recorder writes it: the round-trip cases and the existing `REPLAY_SCHEMA + 1` rejection case all still pass at 3, measured at 0 of the 32 cases replay.test.ts held before the regression coverage. Killed only by the case that names the old version as a literal. REPOINTED 4 -> 5 (issue #797), and the guard now covers that bump too: adding `ReplayMeta.pp1Roles` without moving the constant would accept a schema-4 trace recorded before the arm was carried and rebuild it at shipped caps. The entry keeps its #492 name because the BEHAVIOUR it pins is the same one -- the schema must move whenever the meta shape does -- and renaming the file would strand nothing but make its history harder to follow.
killedBy: checkTrace rejects a schema-4 trace, which predates the recorded pp1Roles arm (issue #797)
